newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MONACO V PSG COULD TURN ON BRAZILIAN FLAIR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MONACO V PSG COULD TURN ON BRAZILIAN FLAIR.

text.p: The French league title hopes of Monaco and Paris St Germain, who meet in a crucial match in the principality on Sunday, depend in no small measure on Brazilian flair.
Anderson, top scorer with 11 goals for his club, has inspired Monaco to the top of the table and the position of favourites for their first championship since 1988.
Former Brazil midfielder Rai would like to win another title with PSG after helping them to the championship in 1994 in his first season in Europe.

And Rai's teammate Leonardo, who, unlike the other two, is a newcomer to Europe this season, took the French league by storm in the autumn, inspiring PSG to the top of the table in an opening 12-match unbeaten run.
"Anderson is a player who has been having some very good seasons in France," Rai said in an interview on Thursday. "I think we are (all three) players who can decide a match."
"The other players know that all Brazilians can do good things in a match.
"Leonardo and I play deeper than Anderson, but we can both come through to score. If we play with only one striker, we try not to leave him alone up front."
Leonardo has scored seven league goals this season and Rai four.
Rai said he, Leonardo and Anderson would be well aware of the duel within the context of a match which PSG cannot afford to lose if they are to stay in the title race with Monaco.

"There have been Brazilian players at Paris St Germain for five or six years," said Rai, who joined PSG from Sao Paulo in 1993 after winning the South American and world club crowns with the Brazilian team.
"The first players who came, like Valdo and (current PSG manager) Ricardo, left a good image, making it possible for others to come and that the club should want to continue working with Brazilians."
Leonardo, looking to win a place in Brazil's 1998 World Cup team in France, signed for PSG in the off-season knowing his chances would be better than in Japan where he was playing.
His presence at the Louis II stadium in Monaco on Sunday, however, is in doubt.
"Ricardo wants him to play if he is fit. He has been unwell," Rai said. "He's a quality player, one of the best at the moment."
Anderson has been in Europe since the early 1990s and in France since 1993 when he joined Marseille from Swiss club Servette. He has never won a Brazil senior cap.
Often linked with a move PSG, something he has said he would like, he refused to talk about Sunday's match.
Rai said he was ready for the clash which follows PSG's traumatic 6-1 home defeat by Juventus in the first leg of the European Super Cup.
"At this time of my career I have to be motived because the future can change so fast. You have to be optimistic," he said.
Rai said he did not think it was possible to win back a place in Brazil's team to defend the World Cup in France next year and he wanted to end his career back home.
